stm32-an3155-p0007-table-00001.luna:
**Table 1. USART bootloader commands**

| Command(footnote) | Command code | Command description |
|---|---|---|
| Get(2) | 0x00 | Gets the version and the allowed commands supported by the current version of the bootloader |
| Get Version & Read Protection Status(2) | 0x01 | Gets the bootloader version and the Read Protection status of the Flash memory |
| Get ID(2) | 0x02 | Gets the chip ID |
| Read Memory | 0x11 | Reads up to 256 bytes of memory starting from an address specified by the application |
| Go | 0x21 | Jumps to user application code located in the internal Flash memory or in SRAM |
| Write Memory | 0x31 | Writes up to 256 bytes to the RAM or Flash memory starting from an address specified by the application |
| Erase(3) | 0x43 | Erases from one to all the Flash memory pages |
| Extended Erase(3) | 0x44 | Erases from one to all the Flash memory pages using two byte addressing mode (available only for v3.0 usart bootloader versions and above). |
| Write Protect(4) | 0x63 | Enables the write protection for some sectors |
| Write Unprotect(4) | 0x73 | Disables the write protection for all Flash memory sectors |
| Readout Protect | 0x82 | Enables the read protection |
| Readout Unprotect(2) | 0x92 | Disables the read protection |

Footnote markers **(2), (3), and (4)** are shown in the table, but the corresponding footnote text is not visible in the provided crop.

stm32-an3155-p0015-figure-00009.luna:

- Decision: **Checksum OK?**
  - **No** → right-side path to **Send NACK byte**, then **End of RM(1)**.
  - **Yes** → **Send ACK byte**
- **Send data to the host**
- **End of RM(1)**

stm32-an3155-p0020-figure-00013.luna:
**Figure 13. Write Memory command: device side** — flowchart for processing the STM32 USART bootloader Write Memory (WM) command.

Visible flow:

1. **Start WM(1)**
2. Decision: **Received byte = 0x31+0xCE?**
   - **No:** branch to the right-side error path, ending in **Send NACK byte**.
   - **Yes:** continue.
3. Decision: **ROP inactive?**
   - **No:** branch to the right-side error path and **Send NACK byte**.
   - **Yes:** continue.
4. **Send ACK byte**
5. **Receive the start address (4 bytes) & checksum**
6. Decision: **Checksum OK?**
   - **No:** branch to the right-side error path and **Send NACK byte**.
   - **Yes:** continue.
7. **Send ACK byte**
8. **Receive the number of bytes to be written (1 byte), the data (N + 1 bytes)(2) and checksum**
9. Decision: **Checksum OK?**
   - **No:** branch to the right-side error path and **Send NACK byte**.
   - **Yes:** continue.
10. Decision: **Flash memory address?**
    - **Yes:** **Write the received data to Flash memory from the start address**; this joins the successful completion path toward **Send ACK byte**.
    - **No:** continue downward.
11. Decision: **RAM address?**
    - **Yes:** **Write the received data to RAM from the start address**; this joins the successful completion path toward **Send ACK byte**.
    - **No:** continue downward.
12. Decision: **Option byte address? & address = 0x1FF F800?**  
    - **Yes:** **Write the Keys for Option byte area access**
      - Then **Write the received data to Option byte area from start address**
      - **Send ACK byte**
      - **Generate system reset**
      - **End of WM(1)**
    - **No:** branch along the bottom completion line to **End of WM(1)**.

The diagram contains two right-side **Send NACK byte** boxes associated with failure paths, and successful Flash/RAM write paths converge on a **Send ACK byte** box before reaching the end. The figure identifier at lower right is **ai14642c**. 

The footnote text for markers **(1)** and **(2)** is not visible in the supplied crop. The option-byte address text is visibly difficult to resolve; it appears as **“0x1FF F800”** in the image.

stm32-an3155-p0022-figure-00014.luna:
**Figure 14. Erase Memory command: host side** — flowchart for the host-side Erase Memory (ER) command.

Flow sequence and branches:

     - **Send checksum**
     - Proceeds to the final ACK/NACK wait stage.
5. Decision: **Wait for ACK or NACK**
   - **NACK**: exits along the right-hand arrow.
   - **ACK**: proceeds downward to **End of ER(1)**.
6. **End of ER(1)**

Visible footnote qualification: **1. ER = Erase Memory.**

stm32-an3155-p0023-figure-00015.luna:
**Figure 15. Erase Memory command: device side** — flowchart for the Erase Memory (ER) command.

Visible text and flow:

- **Start ER(1)**
- Decision: **Received bytes = 0x43+0xBC?**
  - **No** → **Send NACK byte**
  - **Yes** → decision **ROP active**
- Decision: **ROP active**
  - **Yes** → **Send NACK byte**
  - **No** → **Send ACK byte**
- **Receive the number of pages to be erased (1 byte)**
- Decision: **0xFF received?**
  - **Yes** → **Start Global Erase (Mass Erase)**
  - **No** → **Receive the page codes**
- **Receive the checksum**
- Decision: **Checksum OK?**
  - **Yes** → **Erase the corresponding pages** → **Send ACK byte**
  - **No** → **Send NACK byte**
- The **Start Global Erase (Mass Erase)** path proceeds to the ACK response path, bypassing the “Erase the corresponding pages” step.
- The ACK and NACK response paths converge on **End of ER(1)**.

Other visible details:

- Branch labels are **Yes** and **No**.
- Hexadecimal values shown are **0x43+0xBC** and **0xFF**.
- Footnote marker **(1)** appears after **ER** in both “Start ER” and “End of ER.”

stm32-an3155-p0025-figure-00016.luna:
**Figure 16. Extended Erase Memory command: host side** — flowchart for the host-side Extended Erase (EER) command.

Flow sequence and visible text:

1. **Start EER**
2. **Send 0x44 + 0xBB**
3. Decision: **Wait for ACK or NACK**
   - **NACK**: routed along the right-side return path toward the command end.
   - **ACK**: continue downward.
4. Decision: **Special Erase ?**
   - **YES** branch:
     - **Send Special Erase cmd:**
       - **0xFFFF = Mass erase**
       - **0xFFFE = Bank1 erase**
       - **0xFFFD = Bank2 erase**
       - **(0xFFF0 to 0xFFFC are reserved)**
     - **Send the checksum of the two bytes**
   - **NO** branch:
     - **Send the number of pages to be erased N (on two bytes) MSB first**
     - **Send the page numbers (each on two bytes, MSB first)**
     - **Send byte checksum of all sent bytes (N (2 bytes), 2x(N+1) bytes)**
5. The YES and NO branches converge at a second decision: **Wait for ACK or NACK**
   - **ACK**: proceeds downward to **End of EER**
   - **NACK**: follows the right-side return path, which joins the path leading to the end.
6. **End of EER**

Additional visible identifier: **ai17460** at the lower right.

stm32-an3155-p0026-figure-00017.luna:
**Figure 17. Extended Erase Memory command: device side** — flowchart for the Extended Erase Memory (EER) command.

Flow sequence and decision branches:

- **Start EER**
- Decision: **“Received bytes = 0x44 + 0xBB ?”**
  - **NO:** branch right to the NACK path.
  - **YES:** continue downward.
- Decision: **“ROP Active ?”**
  - **YES:** branch right to the NACK path.
  - **NO:** continue downward.
- **Send ACK Byte**
- **Receive Number of Pages to be erased N (2 bytes) MSB first**
- Decision: **“0xFFFF received ? Where Y can be”**
  - **YES:** special-erase path:
    - **Start Special Erase:**
      - **0xFFFF = Mass erase**
      - **0xFFFE = Bank1 erase**
      - **0xFFFD = Bank2 erase**
      - **(0xFFF0 to 0xFFFC are reserved)**
    - **Receive Checksum of the 2 bytes (0x00, 0x02)**
    - Decision: **“Checksum of 2 bytes OK and command supported ?”**
      - **NO:** **Send NACK byte**
      - **YES:** **Perform the requested erase**, then proceed to **Send ACK byte**
  - **NO:** page-erase path:
    - **Receive the page codes (on 2 bytes each, MSB first)**
    - **Receive the checksum of all received bytes N (on 2 bytes), x(N+1) bytes)**
    - Decision: **“Checksum of all received bytes OK”**
      - **NO:** branch right to **Send NACK byte**
      - **YES:** **Erase the corresponding pages**, then **Send ACK byte**

Bottom outputs:

- Left path: **Send NACK byte**
- Center path: **Send ACK byte**
- Right path: **Send NACK byte**
- All three paths converge at the bottom and lead to **End of EER**

Visible figure identifier: **ai17461**.

stm32-an3155-p0029-figure-00019.luna:

stm32-an3155-p0035-table-00002.luna:
**Table 2. Bootloader protocol versions** | Version | Description | |---|---| | **V2.0** | Initial bootloader version. | | **V2.1** | – Update Go command to initialize the main stack pointer
– Update Go command to return NACK when jump address is in the Option byte area or System memory area
– Update Get ID command to return the device ID on two bytes
– Update the bootloader version to V2.1 | | **V2.2** | – Update Read Memory, Write Memory and Go commands to deny access, with a NACK response, to the first bytes of RAM memory used by the bootloader
– Update Readout Unprotect command to initialize the whole RAM content to 0x0 before ROP disable operation | | **V3.0** | – Extended Erase command added to support number of pages larger than 256 and separate bank mass erase.
– Erase command has not been modified in this version but, due to addition of the Extended Erase command it is no longer supported (Erase and Extended Erase commands are exclusive). |
